title: Service Stability: Cornerstone Activation Slate (20w)
content:
Purpose:
This doc lays out a focused 20-week activation slate ("Cornerstone") to operationalize SLOs and service-stability practices across product, serving runtime, platform, and SRE. The goal is to move from concept -> low-friction adoption for 6 pilot services, create repeatable artifacts, and validate the safety-net circuits for automated fallbacks and canary rollouts.

Audience:
- SRE leads and on-call engineers
- Product and feature owners for pilot services
- Platform & Serving Runtime engineering
- Developer Experience and Solutions Eng (for rollout support)

Principles and constraints:
- Ship lift-minimal changes first: focus on signals, clear ownership, and reversible policies.
- Measure first, enforce later: visibility and alerting precede hard policy gates.
- Keep canaries simple: small traffic slices, automated fast rollback triggers, human-in-loop for unknown anomalies.
- Prioritize customer-impact alignment: SLO targets must reflect product-stated promises not purely infra metrics.

Outcome commitments (by week 20):
- 6 pilot services with defined SLOs (availability and latency tiers) and baseline telemetry in observability.
- Runbook templates and one-click canary rollback workflow implemented for partner services.
- Error budget policy examples (gradual throttling, degraded feature flags) implemented for 2 services.
- SDK snippets and onboarding checklist for feature teams (DevX) integrated into service templates.

High-level 20-week plan (phases):
Phase 0 (Weeks 0–2): Alignment & kickoff
- Executive 60-min kickoff + alignment doc.
- Triage pilot service candidates and assign owners.
- Agree on SLO taxonomies and minimal signal set (success rate, p95/p99 latency, circuit errors).

Phase 1 (Weeks 3–8): Observability & measurement baseline
- Instrumentation sprint: ensure each pilot emits the agreed signals.
- Dashboards per service with burn-down and heatmaps.
- Alert tuning: draft alert thresholds that map to error budget consumption.

Phase 2 (Weeks 9–12): Runbooks, playbooks & policy design
- Build runbook templates: incident triage, mitigation, and postmortem checklist.
- Define error-budget actions matrix (e.g., slack channel, throttling stepdown, fallback).
- Draft canary rollout recipe and automated rollback triggers.

Phase 3 (Weeks 13–16): Canary experiments + automated rollback
- Run staged canaries with synthetic and real traffic.
- Validate rollback automation and safety-net (fallthrough to cheaper model variant or region).
- Collect human feedback and iterate on thresholds.

Phase 4 (Weeks 17–20): Handoff, docs, and scale plan
- Finalize onboarding checklist and DevX artifacts (examples, SDK snippets).
- Handoff to Platform/SRE for steady-state operations.
- Post-run retro and readout to stakeholders + next 6-service tranche planning.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Program lead: Aisha Patel — overall accountability, stakeholder sync, and external readout.
- SRE integration owner: Jonah Kim — instrumentation standards, alerts, runbooks.
- Platform automation owner: Marcus Lee — canary plumbing, rollback automation, policy-as-code.
- Product liaison (pilot services): Priya Rao — SLO alignment to product expectations and customer impact.
- Developer Experience: Elena García — templates, SDK snippets, onboarding flow.
- Security & Compliance advisor: Samir Ahmed — review any policy that changes traffic routing or data flow.

Milestones & gating criteria:
- M1 (end wk2): Pilot services chosen + SLO taxonomy approved. Gate: sign-off from product liaisons.
- M2 (end wk8): Baseline telemetry and dashboards in place. Gate: <90% signal coverage triggers remediation plan.
- M3 (end wk12): Runbook and error-budget policy templates ready. Gate: runbooks validated in tabletop exercise.
- M4 (end wk16): Canary rollback automation validated with at least 3 simulated incidents. Gate: rollback <2 min average validated time.
- M5 (end wk20): Handoff complete and retro published. Gate: 6 pilot services onboarded and steady-state playbook accepted.

Communications & cadence:
- Weekly program sync (45m) — core owners only 
- Biweekly stakeholder demo (30m) — wider team + GTM placeholder
- Incident tabletop (wk12) — cross-functional validation of runbooks and SLAs
- Weekly channel updates in #ops-stability with a short status template

Instrumentation & telemetry checklist (minimal signals):
- Request success/failure counts with error classification
- End-to-end request latency (p50/p95/p99) and time-in-queue
- Resource saturation signals (GPU memory, CPU steal, IO) tied to request paths
- Dependency latency and error rates (DB, model-serving nodes, cache)
- Synthetic canary probes and regional health check traces

Runbook & error-budget examples (short):
- Error budget consumption >30% in 24h: increase monitoring frequency, notify product owner, start mitigation play for degraded mode.
- Error budget consumption >60% in 3h: trigger automated throttling policy (traffic-shape or parameterized model fallback) and join SRE-product bridge.

Risk register (top items):
- Insufficient signal coverage on legacy services -> mitigation: fallback to proxy-level metrics and prioritize instrumentation lanes.
- Rollback automation false positives -> mitigation: run synthetic failure tests and require dual-check for non-critical rollbacks.
- Product owners disagree on SLO targets -> mitigation: create a customer-impact mapping doc and run a 1:1 arbitration session.

Success metrics (measurement at week 20):
- Percent of pilot services with SLOs and dashboards: target 100%
- Mean time to rollback for canary failures: target < 2 minutes (automated)
- Number of manual escalations avoided due to error-budget automation: target >= 4 across pilots
- Developer onboarding time (new service to SLO baseline): target < 2 weeks after template adoption

Artifacts to produce:
- SLO spec template (YAML) + examples per service
- Runbook templates and incident checklist
- Canary recipe (traffic split, thresholds, automation code snippets)
- Onboarding checklist and DevX examples repository entry

Open questions & decisions needed:
- Do we require different SLO tiers per customer segment or keep a single service-level target? (Decision owner: Priya)
- What is the minimum automated rollback scope we accept for initial rollout? (Decision owner: Marcus)
- How do we record and expose error budget consumption to customers (if at all)? (Decision owner: Product + Legal)

Immediate next actions (week 0–2):
- Schedule kickoff and invite stakeholder reps (Aisha)
- Rapid inventory for pilot service candidates (Priya + Jonah)
- Draft SLO taxonomy and minimal signal set (Jonah + Marcus)
- Create ephemeral kanban board and assign owners (Aisha)

Notes to self / working thoughts:
- Keep templates intentionally opinionated — frees teams from design paralysis.
- Expect initial friction on latency SLOs for model-related endpoints; plan 2-tier ramping.
- Consider a "safety-net traffic shard" (1% global) for forced rollback validation without real customer impact.

Appendix: example short SLO for a conversation inference endpoint:
- SLI: success_rate = (# requests with generated token stream and 200)/total_requests
- SLO: success_rate >= 99.5% measured over 7d rolling
- Objective: p95 latency < 350ms for prompt length <= 128 tokens, p99 < 700ms
- Error-budget action: at 40% 24h burn -> enable partial fallback to smaller quantized model and throttle long-running batch completions

End of doc.
